Class JdkHttpClientConfiguration.JdkConfiguration

java.lang.Object
io.micronaut.http.client.jdk.JdkHttpClientConfiguration.JdkConfiguration
Direct Known Subclasses:
DefaultJdkHttpClientConfiguration.DefaultJdkConfiguration, ServiceJdkHttpClientConfiguration.ServiceJdkConfiguration
Enclosing interface:
JdkHttpClientConfiguration
public static class JdkHttpClientConfiguration.JdkConfiguration extends Object
The settings under the jdk namespace of a client configuration, only used by the JDK client. All default to false, which keeps the legacy behavior of the JDK client.
Since:
5.3.0

  • Method Details

    • isApplyRequestTimeout

      public boolean isApplyRequestTimeout()
      Whether the JDK client applies the request timeout to an exchange, as the Netty client does. Configured by micronaut.http.client.jdk.apply-request-timeout. Default false: the JDK client only applies the read timeout, until the response headers arrive.
      Returns:
      Whether the JDK client applies the request timeout

    • setApplyRequestTimeout

      public void setApplyRequestTimeout(boolean applyRequestTimeout)
      Parameters:
      applyRequestTimeout - Whether the JDK client applies the request timeout, see isApplyRequestTimeout()

    • isUseMicronautRedirects

      public boolean isUseMicronautRedirects()
      Whether the JDK client follows redirects as the Netty client does, instead of letting the JDK client follow them. Configured by micronaut.http.client.jdk.use-micronaut-redirects. Default false. When enabled, the client filters run for each redirect, the maximum number of redirects and the redirect header settings apply, a 301 or 302 redirect is followed with a GET without the body, a redirect from https to http is followed, and a redirect loop fails with an exception instead of returning the last redirect response.
      Returns:
      Whether the JDK client follows redirects as the Netty client does

    • setUseMicronautRedirects

      public void setUseMicronautRedirects(boolean useMicronautRedirects)
      Parameters:
      useMicronautRedirects - Whether the JDK client follows redirects as the Netty client does, see isUseMicronautRedirects()

    • isDecodeErrorType

      public boolean isDecodeErrorType()
      Whether the HttpClientResponseException of an error status of an exchange of the JDK client decodes the error body into the error type of the exchange, as the Netty client does. Configured by micronaut.http.client.jdk.decode-error-type. Default false: the response of the exception decodes its body into the body type of the exchange, and the error type is not used.
      Returns:
      Whether the JDK client decodes the error body into the error type

    • setDecodeErrorType

      public void setDecodeErrorType(boolean decodeErrorType)
      Parameters:
      decodeErrorType - Whether the JDK client decodes the error body into the error type, see isDecodeErrorType()
